high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Governor: SBV has proactively identified credit growth risks and implemented preventive solutions
high.summary: SBV Governor Nguyen Thi Hong met with Yasuto Watanabe, Executive Director of the ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office (AMRO), highlighting the central bank's proactive approach to credit growth risks. The governor emphasized the effective cooperation between AMRO and Vietnamese agencies, particularly through mid-term consultations, annual consultations, and capacity-building programs including staff secondments and training programs. This signals the SBV's continued focus on macroeconomic surveillance and regional financial cooperation. For FX and bond traders, this suggests the central bank maintains a cautious stance on credit expansion and monetary policy coordination within the ASEAN+3 framework, which could influence future VND liquidity management and policy rates.

high.title: State Bank continues pumping large amounts of VND into market, interbank rates cool down
high.summary: The SBV continued massive VND liquidity injection through OMO operations, offering 65 billion VND (20 billion for 7-day, 30 billion for 14-day, 15 billion for 56-day terms) all at 4.5% annual rate. All amounts were successfully bid. With 50.614 billion VND maturing, the SBV provided net injection of 14.386 billion VND on March 31. Interbank rates responded with overnight rates falling 2.50 percentage points to 9.50%, and 1-week rates dropping 2.80 points to 8.80%. However, longer terms saw increases: 2-week rates up 1.00 point to 8.45% and 1-month up 0.50 points to 8.25%. This aggressive liquidity provision signals the SBV's commitment to supporting banking system liquidity, potentially easing VND funding costs and supporting government bond demand.

high.title: Savings interest rates remain high after State Bank's regulatory warning
high.summary: Despite regulatory warnings from the SBV, deposit rates remain elevated across the banking system. VIB reduced rates by 0.3-0.4 percentage points from peak levels but still offers 7.5-7.6% for large deposits, well above its listed 12-month rate of 7%. Vietbank applies the 4.75% ceiling for short terms but offers up to 7.8% for 12-month deposits. OCB lists rates up to 7.7% for 36-month terms, while Sacombank maintains high promotional rates. This persistent elevation in deposit rates despite regulatory pressure indicates continued competition for funding among banks, which could pressure net interest margins and influence the SBV's monetary policy stance. Bond investors should monitor whether this forces the SBV to maintain accommodative policy longer than planned.

medium.title: VN-Index loses points for 4 consecutive years in April: Will history repeat or be different this time?
medium.summary: VN-Index closed April 1st up 28 points (+1.7%) to reclaim the 1,700 level, raising hopes for a better April performance. Historical data shows April has been a challenging month for Vietnamese equities, with the index declining for four consecutive years. Last year's Trump tariff shock and 2022's major correction from 1,500 peak both began in April. Current market conditions differ significantly from previous years, potentially breaking this negative April pattern.

medium.title: HDBank interest rates for April 2026
medium.summary: HDBank's April 2026 deposit rates range from 0.4% for demand deposits to 8.1% for long-term deposits. Short-term rates (1-2 months) are at 3.5%, while 6-month deposits offer 5.4%. The 12-month term provides 6.1% for regular deposits and up to 8.1% for promotional products, reflecting the continued elevated rate environment across Vietnamese banks.

medium.title: First securities company reveals Q1 2026 business results
medium.summary: Vietcap Securities (VCI) reported estimated Q1 2026 pre-tax profit of 400 billion VND, up 13% year-on-year. The company set ambitious 2026 targets of 6.525 trillion VND revenue and 2.300 trillion VND pre-tax profit, representing 30% and 41% increases respectively. The Q1 result represents about 17% of the full-year profit target.

medium.title: SJC and ring gold prices fell nearly 4 million VND/tael in April 2nd session
medium.summary: Gold prices in Vietnam dropped significantly on April 2nd, with SJC gold bars closing at 170-173.5 million VND/tael (buy-sell), down 3.2-3.7 million VND/tael from the previous session. Ring gold also declined similarly, with prices ranging from 169.8-173.3 million VND/tael across different brands. Prices recovered slightly from intraday lows but remained substantially below the previous day's levels.
